SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall:** The Seller calls its package "negotiated" and "agreed", but nothing here is agreed. It is the Seller's draft. Several positions are one-sided, and the cap and claims period have been moved to our fallback numbers (20% / 18 months) without the written authority from Amelia Frost that we need. A matching number is not clearance.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% figure is our conditional fallback and needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft, which has not been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, excess only recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; restore our figures and tipping-basket mechanics. The Seller's numbers are 5x higher and its excess-only structure removes most small and mid-sized claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a clause applying any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Fundamental/Title claims run at least six years, and fraud sits outside time limits.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter at 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Delete the "applies to all Claims" override, as it would cut across the Title and fraud regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Capping title at 20% on an AUD 24m purchase could leave us uncompensated if we don't own the shares. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Silent. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to all Claims "of any nature", which would catch fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; insert an express carve-out. This is non-waivable and no one on the deal team can trade it away.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Deemed disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject paras 1.1 and 1.2. Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would hollow out the warranties. The specific items in paras 2-10 can be considered as specific disclosures. Para 1.4 (no admission) needs a check so it doesn't undercut the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. If any qualifier is conceded, it needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and delete. "Discoverable" knowledge, combined with whole-data-room disclosure, would effectively neutralise the warranties.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms no consent or evidence of conditions has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002 clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of revenue.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent, with satisfied conditions, a Completion condition. Consent on delivery could be an empty consent that is still subject to unmet conditions.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion". The facility (about AUD 3.2m) has not been repaid and there is no discharge (Disclosure Letter para 3).
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a payout letter and repayment from the proceeds. A post-completion release would only be acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 (DD-005) is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter confirms it is absent and says nothing on on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding of the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. Require an itemised line or a Seller-funded deduction, with on-costs confirmed. The Seller's own words ("a matter for the Seller") support Seller funding, but it must be written down.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity that keeps the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow scope and broaden it to cover wider IP and ownership consequences. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions the transfer of the SOW3 materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 comes from DD-010 and is not independently verified, so don't treat the figure as confirmed in either direction. Ask for payment receipts or a confirmatory assignment.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a proper investigation, and regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric claim in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation. Add covenants on preservation, investigation and updates, and keep the Seller's position on materiality reserved. The Disclosure Letter itself says access, scope and notification are unresolved (about 1,240 records), so we should neither overstate nor dismiss it.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Hold and assess. The Disclosure Letter (para 8) does not support the Seller's "ordinary-course" label. Request the underlying terms (DD-008, DD-011) before deciding anything on price or Debt treatment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Collapses everything into a single general regime ("applies to all Claims"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime").
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept in distinct categories, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete the "applies to all Claims" language at clauses 12.3, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 and draft separate regimes.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as sufficient. DD-012 is an internal Company record, not independent proof, and Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes we have not verified it. Require independent evidence: for example, registry searches, security and charge searches, transfer and authority documents, and confirmation that the Riverlark security does not encumber the shares.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Both kept open, with no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation, and do not concede or assert anything on caps or indemnities in the meantime.

---

## Next steps
1. **Authority:** The 20% cap and 18-month period are available only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. If you want to use them as trades, ask her now. Until then, we hold at 25% / 24 months.
2. **Information requests:** Bluefen consent and conditions; Riverlark payout letter and security release drafts; Ironquay payment evidence; bonus on-cost calculations; Sandbar terms; DD-006 logs and investigation updates; independent title searches.
3. **Mark-up:** I can prepare a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA and a response to the Disclosure Letter on this basis.
